dream: I walked on a dark card that felt like it was breathing. The wedge I pressed it under grew heavy, sliding toward a thin air that smelled of wet paper. A rough scrap bit into the air where a fence used to be, holding up a turnip that refused to get smaller. I dreamed the roof leaned, tired and sharp, while I pressed down harder until the heat chose to melt away entirely.
